close_reason: Landed option (b) — structural round-trip test notification_roundtrip mirroring task_roundtrip and tasklist_roundtrip. Deserialize→serialize→deserialize→Eq tolerates the explicit-null-vs-absent asymmetry on Option<String> + skip_serializing_if fields (documented in workspace AGENTS.md extras-preservation policy). Commit e7afc50. Tasks-types test count: 74 (was 73).
description:
tests/types_test.rs has `notification_deserialize` (line 378) that loads tests/fixtures/notification.json and asserts a handful of fields, but no test re-serializes that notification and compares to the input.

Notification.json contains `"comment": null` (explicit null on an Option<String> field with skip_serializing_if). On deserialize this becomes `None`; on serialize the key is omitted. A naive round-trip test would fail (the input has `comment` as null, the output does not). The absence of a round-trip test masks this asymmetry.

The asymmetry is intentional per workspace AGENTS.md (extras-preservation policy explicitly admits data loss for explicit null vs absent), but the fixture file should not include `"comment": null` if no test exercises it. As written, the explicit-null in the fixture is dead JSON — included for completeness but proving nothing.

Fix options:
  (a) Add a `notification_roundtrip` test that loads the fixture, removes the explicit null, and asserts byte-equal round-trip. (Slightly involved because of the explicit-null/absent mismatch.)
  (b) Add a structural-equality round-trip test that deserializes twice and compares values (Eq), tolerating the null vs absent asymmetry.
  (c) Remove the `"comment": null` line from the fixture and add a structural round-trip.

(b) is the closest analog to the `tasklist_roundtrip` and `task_roundtrip` tests already present and would catch any future TaskNotification deserialize regression. Low cost, high coverage.
title: notification.json fixture is never round-trip tested
